 Semarang Weather Feels Excessively Hot, BMKG Reveals Causes and Today's Temperature Forecast
 BMKG explains why the weather in Semarang feels excessively hot, accompanied by high humidity, along with temperature forecasts and health impacts.
 By: Fadhila Nuraini 
 | 
 Editor: Damar Prasetya 
 | 
 Contributor: Adit Pranata 
 November 16, 2026, 10:27 WITA · 6 min read 
 Photo caption: The atmosphere of Semarang City, Central Java, from the air. Hot weather and high humidity make the air feel even more stifling, especially during the day. (Nadia/Aktualita.co) 
 SEMARANG, Aktualita.co -  The hot weather that often blankets Semarang City, Central Java, has returned to the spotlight due to high air temperatures and humidity in November 2026. Although a number of regions have entered the rainy season, the air during the day still has the potential to feel stinging and cause the body to sweat quickly. 
 Based on the forecast from the Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) for Monday, November 16, 2026, the air temperature in several districts of Semarang City ranges from 24 to 32 degrees Celsius . Relatively high air humidity also makes environmental conditions potentially feel more stifling than the recorded temperature figures. 
 Advertisement 
 This condition is drawing attention because heat can occur simultaneously with the potential for rain. From morning to afternoon, exposure to sunlight can increase surface temperatures, while the growth of rain clouds has the potential to occur at a later time. 
 So, why can Semarang feel so hot even though the air temperature does not always reach extreme levels? 
 BMKG Explains Why Semarang Feels Very Hot 
 The BMKG, through the Central Java Climatology Station, previously reviewed the characteristics of Semarang City's hot temperatures in a popular scientific article published on August 21, 2026. 
 The study explains that the increase in maximum temperature in the Semarang region has a seasonal pattern related to the position of the sun and the transition of seasons. 
 "Data from the BMKG Central Java Climatology Station shows that the peak of monthly maximum temperatures is in March-April and even higher in October-November," wrote Iis Widya Harmoko in an article published by the BMKG Central Java Climatology Station on August 21, 2026. 
 The period from October to November is one of the times when hot conditions can be felt quite strongly. At the same time, air humidity is still high, so the sensation of being stifling is felt even more. 
 Semarang is also a coastal city with dense urban areas. Road surfaces, buildings, and paved areas can absorb solar heat and then release it back into the environment. 
 This phenomenon is one of the factors that can intensify heat exposure in urban areas, especially in locations with limited trees and shaded spaces. 
 33 Degrees Can Feel Like 40 Degrees 
 One of the important things explained by the BMKG is the difference between the actual air temperature and the temperature felt by the human body. 
 In meteorology, this condition is known as heat index . Its calculation considers air temperature and relative humidity to describe the sensation of heat experienced by humans. 
 When humidity is high, sweat is more difficult to evaporate from the skin's surface. In fact, sweat evaporation is the body's natural mechanism for releasing heat. 
 As a result, an air temperature recorded at 33 degrees Celsius under certain conditions can feel close to or even exceed 40 degrees Celsius. 
 In the BMKG's analysis of weather conditions during a running event in Semarang in 2026, air temperatures exceeding 33 degrees Celsius were accompanied by a heat index of up to around 42 degrees Celsius approaching 11:00 AM WIB. 
 However, that figure is the result of an analysis of a previous activity, not a measurement of the heat index of Semarang City on November 16, 2026. 
 This distinction is important because daily temperature forecasts cannot be directly equated with the level of heat felt by someone when active under the sun. 
 Semarang Weather Forecast Today, November 16, 2026 
 Based on BMKG forecast information, most districts in Semarang City have the potential for light to moderate rain on Monday, November 16, 2026. 
 Central Semarang District is forecast to have a temperature of around 26–31 degrees Celsius. Meanwhile, East Semarang is in a similar range with quite high air humidity. 
 In Pedurungan District, the maximum temperature is forecast to reach 32 degrees Celsius. The South Semarang region also has the potential to experience temperatures up to 32 degrees Celsius. 
 Meanwhile, the Banyumanik, Gunungpati, and Mijen areas have relatively lower minimum temperatures, namely around 24 degrees Celsius. 
 Weather conditions can differ between one district and another. Therefore, the public needs to pay attention to forecast updates based on their respective locations. 
 The emergence of potential rain also does not mean that the hot weather automatically disappears. The air can still feel stifling before the rain falls, especially when humidity is high and air circulation is poor. 
 Is Semarang Experiencing a Heatwave? 
 Stifling weather is often associated with the term heatwave . However, the two conditions do not always have the same meaning. 
 The BMKG explains that a heatwave is a phenomenon of temperature increase that is far beyond the normal conditions of a region and lasts for several days. 
 Its determination requires analysis of maximum temperature, climatological averages, and the duration of the event. 
 Therefore, a high temperature on a certain day is not enough to be the basis for stating that a region is experiencing a heatwave. 
 In the context of Semarang, stifling conditions in November can be related to seasonal temperature patterns, high humidity, and urban environmental characteristics. 
 As of the data checked for this article, there is no sufficient observational basis to call the weather in Semarang on November 16, 2026, a heatwave event. 
 Impact of Hot Weather on Health 
 Although not categorized as a heatwave, exposure to high temperatures still requires attention, especially for people who work or are active outdoors for long periods. 
 The Ministry of Health reminds that hot weather can increase the risk of dehydration, fatigue, headaches, and serious health problems if the body is unable to control its internal temperature. 
 Groups that need more attention include children, the elderly, field workers, and people with certain illnesses. 
 Construction workers, drivers, street vendors, and people who exercise during the day are among the groups that have the potential to receive longer heat exposure. 
 If symptoms such as dizziness, weakness, nausea, or excessive sweating appear, activities should be stopped immediately and the body moved to a cooler place. 
 Severe conditions such as confusion, loss of consciousness, or seizures after being exposed to heat require emergency medical assistance. 
 How to Deal with Hot Weather in Semarang 
 The public can take a number of simple steps to reduce the impact of heat exposure. 
 Drinking water regularly is the main step to maintain adequate body fluids. The public is also advised not to wait until they feel very thirsty. 
 Strenuous physical activity outdoors should be reduced during the hottest periods, especially approaching noon to early afternoon. 
 Using light clothing, hats, protection from sunlight, and resting in shaded places can also help reduce direct heat exposure. 
 For people who exercise, choosing the time and adjusting the intensity of training needs to consider weather conditions, humidity, and individual physical abilities. 
 In addition to anticipating heat, Semarang residents still need to prepare equipment to face rain, considering that the BMKG forecast shows the potential for rain in various districts. 
 Changes in weather from hot during the day to rain in the afternoon or evening can occur in the same period. 
 The public is urged to continue paying attention to official BMKG information, especially when planning trips, outdoor work, or sports activities. 
 By understanding the difference between measured temperature and heat index, the public can take more appropriate preventive measures without having to assume every hot weather is a heatwave.
